twoConnectionProbes.name: Positive Determinism & Opposite Input Array Order
twoConnectionProbes.description: Connection 1 passes descending date array [d2, d1] while Connection 2 passes ascending [d1, d2] to SELECT ... ORDER BY calendar_date ASC FOR UPDATE
twoConnectionProbes.observedBehavior: Connection 1 locks d1 then d2; Connection 2 blocks on d1 and times out cleanly with 55P03; after Connection 1 commits, Connection 2 retries and locks both rows without error

twoConnectionProbes.name: Hold Release vs Hold Finalization on Same Hold
twoConnectionProbes.description: Connection 1 locks active booking_holds row FOR UPDATE simulating releaseHold; Connection 2 invokes canonical_finalize_direct_hold
twoConnectionProbes.observedBehavior: Connection 2 blocks on booking_holds (id) row lock before any inventory_days lock is requested; after Connection 1 marks hold RELEASED and commits, Connection 2 cleanly aborts with RESERVATION_HOLD_NOT_ACTIVE with zero inventory mutation

twoConnectionProbes.name: Concurrent Hold Acquisitions on Same Dates
twoConnectionProbes.description: Two connections attempt to acquire hold on same room and dates with limited capacity
twoConnectionProbes.observedBehavior: Both contenders acquire inventory_days in calendar_date ASC order; Connection 2 waits on d1 behind Connection 1; zero deadlock occurs

twoConnectionProbes.name: Calendar Block Creation vs Hold Acquisition
twoConnectionProbes.description: Connection 1 locks inventory_days simulating CalendarService.create; Connection 2 simulates acquireHold with opposite array order
twoConnectionProbes.observedBehavior: Connection 2 blocks on d1 in calendar_date ASC order and times out cleanly; Connection 1 increments blocked_units and commits; zero deadlock cycle

twoConnectionProbes.name: Reservation Cancellation vs Calendar Block Mutation
twoConnectionProbes.description: Connection 1 locks inventory_days simulating canonical_complete_reservation_cancellation (calendar_date ASC, id ASC); Connection 2 simulates calendar block create (calendar_date ASC)
twoConnectionProbes.observedBehavior: Both contenders follow compatible calendar_date ASC order; Connection 2 waits cleanly on d1 behind Connection 1; zero cycle

twoConnectionProbes.name: SQL Itinerary Expiry vs Hold Finalization
twoConnectionProbes.description: Expired hold targeted concurrently by expiry loop and finalizer
twoConnectionProbes.observedBehavior: Expiry worker locks booking_holds FOR UPDATE; finalizer blocks on booking_holds row lock; expiry marks hold EXPIRED and commits; finalizer aborts cleanly with RESERVATION_HOLD_EXPIRED

twoConnectionProbes.name: Multi-Room Future Modifier Simulation (ABBA Demonstration vs Union Sort Resolution)
twoConnectionProbes.description: Simulates concurrent multi-room modifications (Room A -> Room B vs Room B -> Room A) with un-sorted access vs deterministic UNION sort; Probe 7a strictly asserts PostgreSQL 40P01 deadlock with deadlock_timeout = 100ms and lock_timeout = 3000ms
twoConnectionProbes.observedBehavior: Part 7a: Un-sorted room access (Tx 1 locks A then B; Tx 2 locks B then A) triggers PostgreSQL 40P01 deadlock (strictly asserting 40P01, distinguishing from 55P03 lock timeout); Part 7b: Locking UNION(Room A, Room B) sorted deterministically by (calendar_date ASC, room_type_id ASC) converts contending operations into clean serial execution with zero deadlock

twoConnectionProbes.name: Pre-Repair Direct Finalizer vs Payment Composition Lock Inversion (Same Hold + Same Command)
twoConnectionProbes.description: Concurrent race between direct finalizer (Command -> Hold) and pre-repair composition (Hold -> Command) on the same hold H1 and same command C1 with real W1/W2/W3-B fixtures and MATCHED_CAPTURE payment attempt
twoConnectionProbes.observedBehavior: Tx 1 locks canonical_reservation_commands(C1) FOR UPDATE; Tx 2 enters canonical_compose_payment_reservation, locks booking_holds(H1) FOR UPDATE and blocks in finalizer waiting for C1; Tx 1 attempts to lock booking_holds(H1) FOR UPDATE and blocks on Tx 2; PostgreSQL deadlock detector raises 40P01 at 100ms; composition catches 40P01 and records RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED / FINALIZER_FAILURE with details.error_code = '40P01' (or Tx 1 receives 40P01 directly)

auditConclusions.rationale: A pre-repair lock order inversion exists between canonical_finalize_direct_hold (canonical_reservation_commands -> booking_holds) and canonical_compose_payment_reservation (booking_holds -> canonical_reservation_commands). When competing concurrently for the same hold and same target command, PostgreSQL deadlock 40P01 is triggered. Hardening is required via migration 060 to eliminate the pre-finalization booking_holds FOR UPDATE lock from composition.

sharedResourceContract: 1. canonical_reservations (id) FOR UPDATE (Locks reservation root; serializes all concurrent modifications, cancellations, and status transitions on this reservation)
2. canonical_reservation_modification_requests (id) FOR UPDATE (Locks pending C3 intent evidence; verifies unconsumed authorization)
3. stays_quotes / sellable_offers (target_quote_id) FOR SHARE (Freezes target commercial truth and pricing parameters)
4. inventory_days UNION set FOR UPDATE (Deduplicated union of all affected old and new inventory_days rows locked in a single atomic pass)
futureModifierContract.proposedInventorySortKey: ORDER BY calendar_date ASC, room_type_id ASC, id ASC FOR UPDATE
futureModifierContract.unionSortRationale: A deterministic lock of the deduplicated OLD+NEW inventory-day union prevents the demonstrated inventory-row ABBA pattern among writers using that order; it does not establish global cross-resource deadlock freedom.

capacityDriftObservation.rationale: Modifying room_types.inventory_count does not update existing inventory_days.total_units rows, leading to observable capacity drift; however, capacity values only influence numerical availability checks (avail >= quantity) and do not alter row lock acquisition order or the set of locked rows; row locks ensure isolation regardless of total_units values; capacity drift is an inventory accounting concern, not a concurrency lock-order defect
